# OMNI

> OMNI is a deterministic pre-execution trust and risk API for software packages, dependency sets, repositories, and x402 endpoints. It returns advisory assessments with source-attributed evidence; it is not a settlement authority and does not authorize, sign, block, or settle payments.

## Paid API

All four endpoints require x402 payment per request.

- [GET /v1/package/risk](https://omni.example.com/v1/package/risk): package risk assessment ($0.005 USDC). Query: `ecosystem`, `name`, `version`.
- [GET /v1/repo/risk](https://omni.example.com/v1/repo/risk): repository risk assessment ($0.01 USDC). Query: `owner`, `repo`.
- [POST /v1/dependencies/risk](https://omni.example.com/v1/dependencies/risk): per-package assessment for up to 100 packages plus an aggregate summary ($0.05 USDC). Body: `packages[]`.
- [GET /v1/x402/endpoint/preflight](https://omni.example.com/v1/x402/endpoint/preflight): x402 endpoint preflight assessment ($0.01 USDC). Query: `url`.

## Assessment semantics

- `recommendation` is one of `proceed`, `proceed_with_caution`, `manual_review`, `do_not_proceed`. It is advisory output derived from the risk score; it is not an authorization decision, and `do_not_proceed` does not prohibit a payment.
- `riskScore` is an integer 0..100 where higher means more observed decision-relevant risk signals or evidence-source failures.
- `evidenceCoverage` is the 0..1 fraction of evidence paths expected for that subject type that completed successfully. It is not statistical confidence.
- `sourceErrors` lists named upstream sources that failed during the assessment. Treat results with source errors as less complete, not as safe.
- `freshness.expiresAt` is an advisory deadline derived from evidence expiry. Callers should re-run preflight after `expiresAt`; do not silently continue acting on expired evidence.

## x402 endpoint preflight workflow

1. Run preflight on the target resource URL before your agent calls or pays it.
2. The response includes `preflightContext.resource` and `preflightContext.paymentOptions`: every payment option observed from Circle Discovery (`scheme`, `network`, `amount`, `asset`, `payTo`, and `maxTimeoutSeconds` as observed; absent fields are omitted). Observed Circle Gateway metadata is retained under `extra.name`, `extra.version`, and `extra.verifyingContract` when present.
3. After receiving an actual HTTP 402 response from the target, pass its official `PaymentRequired` resource object and the one selected `PaymentRequirements` entry from `accepts[]` to the local consistency helper. It compares `paymentRequired.resource.url` with `preflightContext.resource` and never compares unrelated `ResourceInfo` fields.
4. x402 `PaymentRequirements.amount` is an atomic-unit string. Numeric canonicalization accepts only `^\d+$`; leading zeros may normalize, while decimal fractions and exponent notation never match an integer amount.
5. Consistency outcomes: `match` means the actual requirements match one complete previously observed option; `repreflight_required` means the challenge differs from or postdates the observation; `insufficient_context` means too little was observed to compare meaningfully.
6. A mismatching or stale challenge should trigger a fresh preflight — never automatically mutate or settle a payment.
7. A `match` means only that the payment requirements match the previously observed configuration. It does NOT mean risk-free, sanctioned-clean, authorized, or guaranteed safe.
